attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No nonrelativizing locality-extraction theorem is known that converts an arbitrary small circuit for the real SAT-XOR carrier into a subthreshold label-free incidence transcript; relativizing planted-control examples block the naive argument.
steps: Start with the XOR carrier H_N(x)=<a_N(x),y_N> over F_2 and keep the stable target bridge max{rho,q}<1+epsilon.
Try to replace the direct general-circuit lower bound C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} by hardness against sparse quotient-polynomial sketches.
Any sketch with transcript cost S_T, support A, dimension r, and E errors gives C(H_N)<=S_T+O(A r+E N). This is a valid upper-bound falsifier.
For the reverse direction, if unrestricted quotient transcripts are allowed, choose T(x)=H_N(x), r=1, and P(z)=z. Then SQP_all_N(H_N)<=C(H_N)+O(1).
Thus unrestricted sparse-sketch hardness is equivalent to the original source lower bound and does not reduce the proof burden.
Restricting transcripts to label-free incidence features makes the falsifier meaningful, but the derivation then needs an extraction theorem from arbitrary small H_N circuits to those features.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The target-preserving bridge is valid, but the source lower bound remains exactly the hard general-circuit lower bound unless a structured extraction theorem or direct C(H_N) lower bound is supplied.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: XOR carrier sparse-sketch audit

assumptions: Circuit size is nonuniform and may hardwire constants depending on N and on the real SAT label vector y_N, unless explicitly forbidden.
A point error on an N-bit input can be patched by an equality gate of O(N) size, so E bad inputs cost O(E N).
The transcript class in SQP_all is unrestricted apart from semantic quotient-respect: a_N(x)=a_N(x') implies T(x)=T(x').
definitions: source object: H_N(x)=parity over m_N=N^q generated SAT instances of length L_N=(log N)^d, measured against nonuniform fan-in-2 Boolean circuit size C(H_N).
target object: SAT notin P/poly, obtained only through the separate polylog-query substitution bridge, not from this audit alone.
controlled interface: barely-superlinear source lower bound C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} for infinitely many N versus sparse quotient-polynomial sketches of H_N.
target-preserving condition: d>1, max{rho,q}<1+epsilon, generator cost C(G_N)<=N^rho, and no nonuniform SAT-label leakage inside the generator.
Let a_N(x) be the F_2 incidence vector of the generated formula multiset after parity cancellation, and let y_N(f)=SAT(f).

SQP_all_N(H_N) is the minimum of S_T+A r+E N over arbitrary quotient-respecting transcripts T:{0,1}^N->{0,1}^r of circuit cost S_T and A-sparse F_2 polynomials P with P(T(x))=H_N(x) except on E inputs.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No size-preserving or subexponential fanout-erasure compiler from arbitrary polynomial-size SAT circuits to formulas is known or plausible.
steps: Apply the KW theorem to translate a deterministic communication lower bound c(m) into L_form(SAT_m)>=2^{c(m)}.
To attack SIZE(m^k), compose with a target compiler: every size-s target circuit must have an equivalent formula of size at most F_C(s,m).
For unrestricted circuits use only F_SIZE(s,m)<=2^{O(s)}, so the needed source threshold is c(m)>O(m^k).
But KW communication is at most m+1 by sending the whole yes-input; hence the threshold is impossible for every k>1.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a valid route obstruction, not evidence for P != NP; it only says KW lower bounds must target formulas or low-fanout classes unless a new compiler is supplied.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: KW Fanout-Erasure Gate

assumptions: SAT_m is totalized by rejecting malformed encodings, so KW_{SAT_m} is a standard total-function KW relation.
The target is nonuniform unless a separate uniform formula-simulation certificate is supplied.
For unrestricted circuits the only generic fanout-erasure guarantee used is formula size at most 2^{O(s)}.
The proof object may be non-natural, but fanout leakage is a separate valid obstruction.
definitions: source object: deterministic communication lower bound for the Karchmer-Wigderson relation KW_{SAT_m} of the total m-bit SAT encoding predicate.
target object: De Morgan formula size, or a named circuit class C with an explicit fanout-erasure bound F_C(s,m).
controlled interface: KW theorem plus circuit-to-formula unfolding; reductions preserve the same input length m and do not add padding or advice.
target-preserving condition: the source bound must satisfy c(m)>log_2 F_C(m^k,m) before excluding C-size m^k SAT deciders.

Since D(KW_f)<=m+1 and F_SIZE(s,m)<=2^{O(s)}, the route cannot prove superlinear polynomial circuit lower bounds.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No generated nonblackbox proof currently supplies a sparse, advice-free, non-indexed row source with exact anti-ball soundness and without dense constructive projection.
steps: Let F_m be the generated distinct row set, |F_m|<=2^{D m+o(m)}, N=2^m.
For radius R, bound the projection measure by the union of Hamming ball volumes: mu(B_R(F_m))<=|F_m| Vol(N,R)/2^N.
For R=N^rho with rho<1, Vol(N,R)<=2^{O(N^rho log N)}, hence mu<=2^{-N+o(N)}; this is far below 2^{-poly(m)} and therefore non-large.
The existing multiplexing extraction from an actual generated hard row remains unchanged: padded rank/address inputs give delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)).
Try to repair locatability by replacing F_m with a dense decidable U_m containing F_m and excluding all small circuits.

If U_m has measure at least 2^{-poly(m)} and P/poly(N) constructivity, then U_m is a useful natural property against SIZE(2^{theta m}); this collides with the natural-proofs barrier under standard PRF assumptions.

If U_m is obtained by sublinear fattening, it avoids largeness but still does not provide a selector for a hard center. If it is obtained by near-half fattening, anti-ball soundness for centers does not imply soundness for all of U_m.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation only separates valid sparse transfer from invalid dense locator repairs. It does not construct the required generated anti-ball carrier and gives no unconditional P != NP consequence.

assumptions: The carrier row set F_m has distinct-image entropy D: |F_m|<=2^{D m+o(m)}.
Every generated row is proved outside the Hamming ball of every circuit of size below 2^{theta m}; exact MCSP extraction uses the row itself, not the fattened set.
The generator and unranking are E-uniform and advice-free; proof streams may be exponentially long but are deterministically locatable from m and rank.
The target consequence is route-level E lower bounds, not a proof of P != NP.
definitions: source object: a deterministic advice-free generator G_m that emits at most 2^{D m+o(m)} truth tables T_{m,j} of length N=2^m together with generated nonblackbox anti-ball proofs against circuits of size s_m=2^{theta m}.
target object: the E-uniform multiplexed language L_G whose input encodes a padded length m, a row rank j, and an address x, with desired unrestricted circuit lower bound 2^{delta n}.
controlled interface: E-canonical unranking of distinct generated rows, sequential proof generation, no subthreshold indexed row decoder, and no nonuniform locator for hard rows.
target-preserving condition: for kappa-dense source lengths and image entropy D, the transfer is valid only when theta is below the verifier leakage cap and delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)).
Hamming fattening B_R(F_m) is the union of radius-R Hamming balls around the generated row set F_m in {0,1}^N.
Natural-size projection means measure at least 2^{-poly(m)} inside {0,1}^N and decidability by circuits polynomial in N.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier-calibration bridge lemma: it preserves the valid sparse carrier transfer while showing that dense locator repairs would become natural proofs, not hidden MCSP extraction.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Low-image generated anti-ball MCSP carriers are quantitatively non-large under every sublinear Hamming fattening, while any polynomial-time decidable dense projection that still excludes small circuits is exactly a Razborov-Rudich-style natural useful property. Thus projection/locator repair must remain sparse and non-indexed, or it becomes a barrier object rather than a target-preserving carrier.

assumptions: R=N^rho for fixed rho<1.
F_m has at most 2^{D m+o(m)} centers.
The route needs exact hard rows for MCSP extraction, not merely nearby tables.
definitions: Fattened locator U_{m,R}=B_R(F_m).
Decoder leakage means a circuit can recover enough of a center T_{m,j} from a short rank, interval, or nearest-center procedure to compute T_{m,j} with size below 2^{theta m}.
Selector validity requires E-uniform generation of the chosen row, not existential membership in U_{m,R}.

candidate_lemmas.statement: Sublinear Hamming fattening of a low-D anti-ball carrier cannot make the source naturally findable: its measure remains 2^{-N+o(N)}. It may preserve non-largeness, but it gives no new selector unless membership or nearest-center recovery is added, and that recovery risks decoder leakage.

assumptions: Centers are sparse: |F_m|=2^{O(m)}.
No pseudorandomness assumption is used to prove the measure calculation.
The route refuses nonuniform advice selecting only hard centers.
definitions: Near-half expansion means radius N/2-O(sqrt(N poly(m))) around sparse centers.
Soundness collapse means U_m contains a truth table of circuit size below 2^{theta m}.
Global exclusion theorem would prove every point of the large projection avoids all small circuits, not just the generated centers.

candidate_lemmas.statement: To obtain natural largeness from only 2^{O(m)} centers, a projection must expand to near-half Hamming radius. Such expansion is not certified by positive-radius anti-ball proofs against small circuits and is expected to intersect easy truth tables, so it cannot be used as an MCSP no-side source without a new global exclusion theorem.
